function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below are several common ways to pull *detailed* information for a specific network interface, depending on the platform and the tools you have at hand. | Platform / Tool | Typical command / API call | What it returns (key fields) | Notes | |-----------------|----------------------------|------------------------------|-------| | **Cisco IOS / IOS‑XE / IOS‑XR** | `show interface ` (e.g., `show interface GigabitEthernet0/1`) | • Interface status (up/down)
• MAC address
• MTU, speed, duplex
• Input/output counters (bytes, packets, errors, discards)
• Physical layer details (line protocol, transceiver type, link partner capabilities) | Use `show interface detail` for even more verbose output (e.g., line protocol state, hardware type). | | **Cisco NX‑OS** | `show interface | include all` | Same as above, but NX‑OS uses slightly different wording. | | | **Juniper Junos** | `show interfaces extensive` (or `show interfaces detail`) | • Interface status
• MAC address
• MTU, speed, duplex
• Counters (in/out bytes, packets, errors, discards)
• Physical layer info (link mode, auto‑negotiation, transceiver type) | `show interfaces terse` gives a quick summary; `extensive` gives full detail. | | **Linux / Unix** | `ip -s link show ` or `ifconfig -a` | • Interface state (UP/DOWN)
• MAC address
• MTU, speed (if available)
• Counters (rx/tx bytes, packets, errors, dropped, overruns, frame errors) | `ethtool ` can provide driver, firmware, link partner details. | | **Windows** | `Get-NetAdapter -Name "" | Format-List *` (PowerShell) | • Status, MAC, speed, duplex, driver info, statistics | | | **SNMP** | OID `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8.` (ifOperStatus) + other OIDs (`ifDescr`, `ifPhysAddress`, `ifInOctets`, `ifOutOctets`, etc.) | Numeric values; you’ll need to map OIDs to human‑readable names. | Use an SNMP client (e.g., `snmpwalk`, `snmpget`). | | **RESTCONF / NETCONF** | `/restconf/data/interfaces/interface=` (RESTCONF) or `/netconf/` (NETCONF) | XML/JSON representation of the interface configuration and operational state. | Requires the device to expose a RESTCONF or NETCONF endpoint. | | **Device Connector API** | If your device exposes a custom API, you might call something like `GET /api/interfaces/` | Depends on vendor; usually JSON with status, counters, config. | Use the vendor’s SDK or documentation. | --- ### Quick‑start examples #### Cisco IOS ```bash # Show all details for GigabitEthernet0/1 show interface GigabitEthernet0/1 detail ``` #### Juniper Junos ```bash # Show extensive details for ge-0/0/1 show interfaces ge-0/0/1 extensive ``` #### Linux ```bash # Show stats for eth0 ip -s link show eth0 # Or use ethtool for driver & link partner ethtool eth0 ``` #### SNMP (using snmpwalk) ```bash snmpwalk -v2c -c public 192.168.1.1 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1 ``` #### RESTCONF (curl example) ```bash curl -k -u admin:admin https://192.168.1.1/restconf/data/interfaces/interface=GigabitEthernet0%2F1 ``` --- ### Things to keep in mind 1. **Permissions** – You’ll need privileged access (e.g., enable mode on Cisco, root on Linux, or appropriate SNMP community string). 2. **Interface naming** – Make sure you’re using the correct name (e.g., `GigabitEthernet0/1`, `ge-0/0/1`, `eth0`, `ens33`). 3. **Speed & Duplex** – Some platforms report negotiated speed/duplex; others may show the configured value. 4. **Counters** – Most counters are cumulative since last reboot; you’ll need to read them over time to calculate rates. 5. **Transceiver info** – On many devices you can get SFP/CMIS module details (vendor, serial number, temperature) via `show interface transceiver` or `ethtool -m`. --- If you let me know which device or operating system you’re working with, I can give you a more tailored command or API call.
